title: Migrator role is not documented on-chain — natspec on stakeFor/unstakeFor/withdrawRewardToken does not state the trust assumption
description: The plan models the migrator (via MigrationHelper) as 'no admin, no upgrade path. Holds no funds between txs.' This is a strong claim about the trust model. The on-chain documentation only says (line 80-82): 'Address authorised to call stakeFor/unstakeFor and (jointly with the owner) withdrawRewardToken. Settable by owner via setMigrator. address(0) disables all migrator-gated functions.' This describes WHAT the migrator can do, not WHO the migrator is supposed to be. A user reading the source code sees a privileged role that can (a) pull NFTs from any beneficiary's stake (line 558), (b) drain the reward token when paused and totalStaked == 0 (line 564). There is no on-chain hint that this role is intended to be a stateless, restricted helper. If a future deployer reads the source and concludes the migrator is a general-purpose admin slot, they may assign it to a multisig or EOA — breaking the plan's trust model without realising it.
impact: Documentation drift between off-chain plan and on-chain code. A future deployer (or auditor) cannot derive the trust model from the source alone. This is the inverse of the standard `Ownable` situation, where the trust model is widely understood — the `migrator` role is a project-specific concept with no established norms.
recommendation: Expand the natspec on `migrator` (line 79-83) and on each migrator-gated function to state the intended trust assumption: 'In production this role is held by the MigrationHelper contract — a stateless, single-purpose contract with no admin and no upgrade path. Assigning this role to a multisig, EOA, or any contract holding state across calls expands the trust surface beyond the migration plan's design.' Cross-reference the plan or a checked-in design doc.
attack_scenario: Not directly attackable. The risk is operational/governance: a future deployer following the on-chain documentation alone (without the plan) sets `migrator` to a general admin multisig, then that multisig can do everything documented above. The current deployment is presumably correct; the concern is downstream deployments or re-uses of NFTStakerV2 in other contexts.
